newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul tightens rules on issue of convertible bonds.
newsitem.headline: Seoul tightens rules on issue of convertible bonds.

text.p: South Korea's finance ministry said on Wednesday that starting April it would ban issues of privately-placed convertible bonds (CBs) during disputes over managerial rights.
Such bonds would not be able to be converted into stocks for a year to prevent companies from using the issues as defence against hostile takeover bids.
The ministry said in a statement these moves were aimed at protecting minor shareholders during managerial disputes.
Controlling shareholders currently are able to issue CBs to increase their stake, the ministry said.
The ministry added that the conversion price should not be below the market price of existing shares.
Currently, there are no rules on pricing.
The conversion price for publicly placed convertible bonds would be raised to 100 percent of existing share prices or higher from the current bottom limit of 90 percent.

Issues of publicly placed CBs would be limited to firms which gave out an average of 200 won or more per share in dividend payments for the past three years. Such issues would be limited to within 50 percent of share capital, the ministry said.
